title: An epidermis’s physical characters follow simply from its lying on the outside

fields.label: Label
fields.value: An epidermis’s physical characters follow simply from its lying on the outside

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The fundamental character of an epidermis is that it lies on the outside of the cell mass, and its main physical features (flattened, rectangular cells meeting partitions at near right angles) follow from that position through unequal and consolidated tensions in its outer walls.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. VII: The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: the fundamental character of an epidermis simply is that it lies on the outside, and that its main physical characteristics follow, as a matter of course, from the position which it occupies and from the various consequences which that situation entails.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter VII, “The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates”; topic “Epidermal layer as a positional effect”. Scope: epidermal tissue of plants (especially simple epidermal tissue as in Laminaria) and analogous outer cell layers

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch07-07: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.57

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The geometric correlates are measurable, but 'follow as a matter of course' demands causal separation of position from differentiation. Existing comparative images support association tests, not a clean general mechanistic verdict.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare outer and internal cells with matched lineage and perturb position, testing whether exterior location predicts flattening, rectangularity, and near-right-angle partitions through measured wall mechanics.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Few public datasets include position swaps and wall-tension measurements.

Outer position covaries with cell identity and gene expression.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Outer versus inner cell shape is directly measurable in open embryo and meristem segmentations, so the positional pattern can be tested. The claim also says the physical features follow from that position through unequal, consolidated tensions, which the images do not measure. Identity programs remain a live alternative for the same flattened outer layer.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare outer-layer cells with interior cells for flattening, rectangular outline and near-right angles at the outer wall, and ask whether those traits track position alone. Outer cells showing that suite because they lie outside, including after identity programs are perturbed, would support the claim; an epidermal shape program that appears independent of outside position would limit it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Position and epidermal identity are usually confounded, and these geometry sets do not include the identity-perturbation experiments.

Laminaria-type simple thalli are not in the Arabidopsis-heavy archives.
